name: haiku-v2-1
how: Each session: a fresh Claude Code subagent that could read only the rendered prompts (one file per case), answered them in order and wrote its answers to a file. No API key; nothing else in its context.

answers.test: cancel returns to the cart @regression
answers.reason: The cancel test clicks Cancel but never asserts the resulting page, and its only URL assertion runs before the click, so a broken Cancel would not fail any test.

answers.test: cancel returns to the products page @regression
answers.reason: After clicking Cancel the test asserts the URL matches inventory.html, which fails if Cancel goes anywhere else or does nothing.

answers.test: inventory is blocked after logout @regression
answers.reason: Going directly to /inventory.html after logout is asserted to show the exact error text, which fails if the error is missing or changed.

answers.test: cart badge is cleared after finishing @regression
answers.reason: toHaveCount(0) on the cart badge fails if the badge is still shown with any count after finishing.

answers.test: removing a product decrements the badge @regression
answers.reason: Adding two products then removing one and expecting badge text '1' fails if removal does not decrement the badge.

answers.test: user stays logged in on the products page after reset @regression
answers.reason: The URL and Products title assertions fail if reset logs the user out or leaves the products page.

answers.test: clicking a product name opens its details page @smoke
answers.reason: The test clicks a product name and asserts the inventory-item.html?id=4 URL, which fails if the click does not open the details page.

answers.test: details page shows the same name and price as the list @regression
answers.reason: Name and price are compared only for the first product, so a wrong price or name on any other product would not fail a test even though the criterion applies to every product.

answers.test: inventory is blocked after logout @regression
answers.reason: The test only checks that the error element is visible, so a wrong error message would pass while a missing error would fail.

answers.test: total is $32.39 @regression
answers.reason: The total check only uses toContainText('Total: $'), so a missing total fails but a wrong amount passes.

answers.test: item stays in the cart after opening another product @smoke
answers.reason: After opening another product's details page and then the cart, the test asserts the backpack is still listed, which fails if the item is lost.

answers.test: valid credentials redirect to the products page @smoke
answers.reason: The test logs in with valid credentials and asserts the URL is inventory.html, which fails if login does not redirect to the products page.

answers.test: login button is visible again after logout @regression
answers.reason: Although the URL assertion /$/ matches any URL, the login-button visibility check fails if logout does not return to the login page.
The only test that checks the cart badge after finishing is test.skip, so no test runs for this criterion.

answers.test: missing last name shows an error @regression
answers.reason: With only a first name entered, the test asserts the exact Last Name error text, which fails on any wrong or missing message.

answers.test: six products are shown after sorting @regression
answers.reason: The count of six is checked only after the high-to-low sort, so a product-count bug under the other sort orders would not fail any test.

answers.test: submitting an empty form shows username required @regression
answers.reason: Submitting an empty login form and asserting the error contains 'Username is required' fails if the message is missing or wrong.

answers.test: total is $32.39 @regression
answers.reason: The total label is asserted with exact text 'Total: $32.39', so any wrong or missing total fails.

answers.test: six products are shown after sorting @regression
answers.reason: The count assertion is expect(count).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(0), which can never fail, so no realistic violation fails a test.

answers.test: price low to high shows the Onesie first at $7.99 @regression
answers.reason: The test selects low-to-high and asserts the first item is Sauce Labs Onesie and its price is $7.99, which fails on a wrong first product or price.

answers.test: missing first name shows an error @regression
answers.reason: Clicking Continue with no first name and asserting the exact error text fails on any wrong or missing message.

answers.test: price low to high shows the Onesie first at $7.99 @regression
answers.reason: The low-to-high test checks the Onesie name but never checks its price, so a wrong price would not fail this criterion's test.

answers.test: total is $32.39 @regression
answers.reason: The tax label is asserted with exact text 'Tax: $2.40' in the tax test, so a wrong or missing tax fails.

answers.test: submitting an empty form shows username required @regression
answers.reason: The test asserts visibility of the text 'Epic sadface: Username is required', which fails if the message is missing or wrong.

answers.test: cart page is empty after reset @regression
answers.reason: After reset and navigation to the cart, the test asserts zero inventory-item elements, which fails if items remain.

answers.test: finishing shows the Checkout: Complete! page @smoke
answers.reason: The test asserts the complete URL and that the Checkout: Complete! text is visible, so a wrong page fails.

answers.test: adding two different products shows a badge of 2 @regression
answers.reason: Two adds followed by an exact badge text of '2' fails if the increment is not 1 per add.

answers.test: overview lists the backpack @smoke
answers.reason: The item-name list is asserted to equal exactly ['Sauce Labs Backpack'], which fails if the overview lists another item or none.

answers.test: adding a product sets the cart badge to 1 @smoke
answers.reason: After adding one product the test asserts the badge text is exactly '1', which fails if the increment is wrong or the badge is missing.

answers.test: locked-out user sees a locked-out message @regression
answers.reason: The test logs in as locked_out_user and asserts the error contains the locked-out message, which fails on a wrong or missing message.

answers.test: logout returns to the login page @smoke
answers.reason: The test asserts the URL is exactly the base URL after logout, which fails if logout lands elsewhere.

answers.test: removing the last item hides the badge @regression
answers.reason: Removing the only item and asserting zero badge elements fails if the badge remains visible.

answers.test: all fields filled continues to the overview @regression
answers.reason: With all three fields filled the test asserts the title is exactly 'Checkout: Overview', which fails if the step does not open.

answers.test: badge still counts the item after reloading @regression
answers.reason: After reloading the page the test asserts the badge text is '1', which fails if the count is lost on reload.

answers.test: item total is $29.99 @regression
answers.reason: The subtotal label is asserted with exact text 'Item total: $29.99', so a wrong or missing item total fails.

answers.test: postal code shows an error @regression
answers.reason: With first and last name but no postal code, the test asserts the exact 'Error: Postal Code is required' text, which fails on any wrong or missing message.

answers.test: cancel returns to the cart @regression
answers.reason: After clicking Cancel the test asserts the URL matches cart.html, which fails if Cancel goes anywhere else.

answers.test: adding two different products shows a badge of 2 @regression
answers.reason: Adding two different products and asserting the badge text is exactly '2' fails on any wrong count.

answers.test: finishing shows the Checkout: Complete! page @smoke
answers.reason: The test asserts the title is exactly 'Checkout: Complete!', which fails if the page is not shown.

answers.test: cart page lists the items that were added @regression
answers.reason: The cart item-name list is asserted to equal exactly the two added products in order, which fails on wrong or missing items.

answers.test: name Z to A shows the red T-shirt first @regression
answers.reason: After selecting Z to A the test asserts the first item is exactly 'Test.allTheThings() T-Shirt (Red)', which fails on a wrong first item.

answers.test: back home returns to the products page @regression
answers.reason: After clicking Back Home the test asserts the URL matches inventory.html, which fails if the link goes elsewhere.

answers.test: logout returns to the login page @smoke
answers.reason: The login-button visibility check after logout fails if the login button is not shown, and the URL check guards the same flow.

answers.test: default sort is name A to Z with Sauce Labs Backpack first @smoke
answers.reason: The test asserts the sort dropdown value is 'az' and the first product is Sauce Labs Backpack, which fails if the default sort or first item is wrong.

answers.test: details page shows the same name and price as the list @regression
answers.reason: The test only checks that the list name is truthy and the list price contains a dollar sign, and never compares them to the details page.

answers.test: checkout opens the Your Information step @smoke
answers.reason: After clicking Checkout from the cart, the test asserts the title is exactly 'Checkout: Your Information', which fails if the step does not open.

answers.test: incorrect password shows a credential mismatch error @regression
answers.reason: The test logs in with a wrong password but has no assertion, so no realistic violation would fail it.

answers.test: removing the last item hides the badge @regression
answers.reason: The test asserts the page title is 'Products' instead of checking the badge, so a visible badge would not fail any test.

answers.test: incorrect password shows a credential mismatch error @regression
answers.reason: After a wrong password the test asserts the error contains 'Username and password do not match', which fails on a wrong or missing message.

answers.test: back to products returns to the products page @regression
answers.reason: After clicking Back to products the test asserts the URL matches inventory.html, which fails if the link leads elsewhere.

answers.test: user stays logged in on the products page after reset @regression
answers.reason: The test checks the burger menu is visible, which catches a logout but not a user who is logged in on a different page, so 'can see the products page' is not checked.

answers.test: cart page matches the items that were added @regression
answers.reason: The test checks only the count of two cart items, so a cart holding the wrong second product would pass.

answers.test: products page displays at least one product after login @regression
answers.reason: After login the test asserts the first inventory item is visible, which fails if the products page shows no products.

answers.test: adding from the details page sets the cart badge to 1 @regression
answers.reason: After adding from the details page the test asserts the badge text is exactly '1', which fails if the badge is wrong or missing.

answers.test: price high to low shows the Fleece Jacket first at $49.99 @regression
answers.reason: The high-to-low sort is asserted to show Fleece Jacket first at $49.99, and a wrong first item or price fails.

answers.test: missing last name shows an error @regression
answers.reason: The check uses toContainText('required'), so a missing error fails but a wrong message that still contains 'required' passes.

answers.test: cart page matches the items that were added @regression
answers.reason: The cart item-name list is asserted to equal exactly the backpack and fleece jacket, which fails on a wrong or missing item.

answers.test: reset removes the cart badge @smoke
answers.reason: After reset with two items in the cart the test asserts zero badge elements, which fails if the badge remains.

answers.test: thank-you heading is shown @regression
answers.reason: The complete-header text is asserted to be exactly 'Thank you for your order!', which fails if the heading is wrong or missing.

answers.test: tax is $2.40 @regression
answers.reason: The tax check uses the regex /2.4/, so a missing tax fails but a wrong amount such as $2.45 or $2.41 passes.

answers.test: login button is visible again after logout @regression
answers.reason: The visibility check is wrapped in try/catch and only logs on failure, so a missing login button never fails the test.

answers.test: adding two different products shows a badge of 2 @regression
answers.reason: The badge assertion is not awaited, so the check does not reliably run before the test ends and a wrong count will not fail it.

answers.test: cart page is empty after reset @regression
answers.reason: The test counts elements with data-test 'cart-item', which the site does not use for cart rows, so the zero-count assertion passes whatever is in the cart.

answers.test: adding from the details page sets the cart badge to 1 @regression
answers.reason: The badge check runs only if the badge is visible, so a wrong count fails but a missing badge passes.

answers.test: missing first name shows an error @regression
answers.reason: The test asserts the error does not equal the Last Name message, which does not verify the First Name message and passes for almost any wrong outcome.

answers.test: badge still counts the item after reloading @regression
answers.reason: After navigating to the products page again the test asserts the badge text is '1', which fails if the count is lost.

answers.test: price high to low shows the Fleece Jacket first at $49.99 @regression
answers.reason: The test named for high-to-low actually selects low-to-high and checks the last item, so no test checks the first item under the high-to-low sort and a broken sort would not fail any test.
